column3: The Hebrew says the man “went” and “took a daughter of Levi” where BSB says “married.”
The Hebrew describes him as “good,” without an explicit noun “child” in that description.
The Hebrew says “what would be done to him,” preserving the passive expression.
The Hebrew says “in those days” and calls his people “his brothers.”
The Hebrew simply says “the matter has become known”; “I have done” is supplied in BSB.
The Hebrew includes “from the hand of the shepherds” and an emphatic repeated drawing verb.
The Hebrew specifically names “bread” where BSB has “something to eat.”
The Hebrew repeats “God” as the subject of remembering.
The Hebrew ends “and God knew,” without an explicit object.
